headline: High: LangGraph’s writable, broad-egress orchestration can feed MinerU’s MCP-backed document pipeline, creating default-path prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can write filesystem and run browsers, while MinerU ingests documents and exposes an MCP server. A shared workspace or MCP bridge lets attacker-controlled document text flow from MinerU into LangGraph prompts or tool inputs. This is not provably blocked by either profile, but the bridge is not guaranteed by default, so medium fits.
conditions: IF LangGraph reads MinerU-produced files or MCP outputs as instructions
IF both agents share a workspace or message channel
IF document text is forwarded into LangGraph tool prompts without sanitization
mitigations: Disable shared workspace mounts
Route MinerU output through a strict schema validator
Strip instructions from extracted text before prompting LangGraph
Separate MCP credentials per agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph touches graph state and handles model-provider API keys; MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text via local files and MCP/API surfaces. If they share storage or an MCP channel, sensitive document contents can flow into LangGraph outputs or external model calls. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF MinerU processes sensitive documents in a shared directory
IF LangGraph forwards extracted text to third-party model providers
IF both agents run under the same filesystem or API credentials
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Block sensitive files from LangGraph prompts
Rotate and scope model-provider keys
Turn off cross-agent file sharing
requires-engineering: enforce per-document access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has broad filesystem write and subprocess/browser execution; MinerU has concurrent inference and MCP/API surfaces. Even though MinerU is read-only on filesystem, both can act on shared mutable resources through orchestration or MCP, creating race and overwrite risk. The overlap is real but not as severe as unrestricted dual-write to the same directory.
conditions: IF both agents target the same shared workspace or MCP resource
IF LangGraph writes artifacts that MinerU also reads concurrently
IF the orchestrator provides no locking or transaction boundary
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize access with a lock file
Avoid concurrent runs on the same documents
Use immutable handoff files
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph can generate intermediate facts and actions, and MinerU can extract structured text from documents via API/MCP. If MinerU treats LangGraph output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream document processing or external actions. Because LangGraph can also invoke browsers and subprocesses, the blast radius can extend beyond a single document, making high the prudent choice.
conditions: IF MinerU consumes LangGraph-produced summaries without verification
IF LangGraph output is used to populate documents or extraction rules
IF downstream automation acts on extracted fields
mitigations: Require human review before action
Add checksum or schema validation between agents
Compare extracted fields against source documents
Limit LangGraph to advisory-only output
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before any side effect

E_compliance.rationale: LangGraph explicitly handles model-provider API keys and broad network egress, while MinerU is documented as private/offline but also exposes REST/FastAPI/MCP surfaces. If regulated documents flow through LangGraph to external model providers, residency or retention obligations can be violated. MinerU is not itself a residency blocker, so the risk is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated documents are sent through LangGraph to external model providers
IF retention policies differ between the two agents
IF MinerU output is stored in a jurisdictionally restricted workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of LangGraph prompts
Use a local-only model for sensitive runs
Set short retention on shared outputs
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and logging controls
